name: Southend-on-Sea

licensing.selective: Selective licensing covers designated neighbourhoods in Milton, Kursaal, Victoria and Chalkwell wards from 1 December 2021 until 30 November 2026. The council is consulting (until 31 December 2026) on a renewed and larger scheme, possibly from 1 April 2027, so there will be a gap after the current scheme ends.
licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme; the council says it is exploring whether one could help. HMOs with five or more people from two or more households need a mandatory licence.

housing: Southend-on-Sea is a seaside city at the mouth of the Thames, and more than a quarter of households rented privately in 2021. The central wards have many Victorian and Edwardian houses split into flats and flats over shops, which is where selective licensing applies. Leigh-on-Sea, Chalkwell and Thorpe Bay have larger Edwardian and inter-war homes, and the outer areas are mostly post-war bungalows and semis. It is a commuter town for London on two railway lines.
checkinTips: Victorian and Edwardian houses split into flats in Westcliff and Victoria: note which rooms, gardens and storage belong to the flat, and photograph the communal hall, meters and fire doors.
Seafront homes: check window frames, balconies, outside paint and metal fittings for salt and wind damage.
Flats over shops in the town centre: photograph the street door, stairs, smoke alarms and the escape route.
Homes in the selective licensing areas: check the licence and note its number in the report, and watch for the change when the scheme is renewed.
Bungalows in Eastwood and Southchurch: record gardens, fences, garages and driveways, which tenants are often expected to keep up.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems can contact Southend-on-Sea City Council's private sector housing team, which inspects privately rented homes and enforces the licensing scheme.
